texts: Untreated patients with pulmonary atresia and intact ventricular septum have a mortality approaching 85 percent at 6 months: B.
The lungs depend on the ductus, so when it closes the infant dies unless prostaglandin and an intervention follow.
The plan rests on the size of the right ventricle and tricuspid valve and on the coronary circulation, not on the degree of hypertrophy.
Fistulas from the right ventricle to the coronary arteries are most common with a small, hypertensive right ventricle and a competent tricuspid valve, and an Ebstein-like tricuspid valve can occur.
In the picture, when the duct-tape tunnel closes untreated, 85 babies in 100 lie in coffins by six months.
Memory hook: a welded door and a closing tunnel: 85 in 100 by six months.
